name: Ailoquence Connector
author: ailoquence

sections.description:
Ailoquence is an AI content platform for blogs, social media and online stores. This plugin connects your WordPress site to your Ailoquence account so you can:

  • Publish and schedule blog posts written in Ailoquence, with their featured image, categories and tags. Posts are scheduled in your site’s own time zone.
  • Update a post you already published from Ailoquence, instead of creating a duplicate.
  • Keep the SEO title, meta description, keywords and social sharing tags written in Ailoquence. They are saved in Yoast SEO, Rank Math or All in One SEO if you use one of them; otherwise the plugin adds them to the page itself.
  • Import your existing posts into Ailoquence.
  • Link your WooCommerce store so Ailoquence can create content from your products.

An Ailoquence account is required. Sign up, or log in if you already have one. The plugin does nothing on its own: it receives requests from Ailoquence and, if you choose to, sends your store credentials to Ailoquence.

Security

  • Every request from Ailoquence is signed with HMAC-SHA256 using a secret generated on your site that you share only with your Ailoquence account. Requests older than 5 minutes are rejected.
  • You can turn off all incoming requests with a single checkbox, restrict them to specific IP addresses, and regenerate your credentials at any time.
  • The WooCommerce key the plugin creates is revoked when you disconnect the store or uninstall the plugin.

External services

This plugin connects to the Ailoquence API (https://api-pro.ailoquence.com), a service provided by Ailoquence.

The plugin contacts Ailoquence in these cases only. Publishing and importing posts work the other way round, with Ailoquence sending signed requests to your site.

  1. Connecting the store: when an administrator clicks “Connect my store automatically”. What is sent: your site’s URL, a WooCommerce REST API key (consumer key and secret, read/write access) created for this purpose, the plugin’s Public Key, and the Store Public Key and Store Secret shown on the settings page. They are used to link your store to your Ailoquence project so it can read your products and apply the changes you make to them from Ailoquence.
  2. Email alerts setting: when an administrator saves the “Email alerts from Ailoquence” setting. What is sent: whether alerts are enabled, signed with the Store Secret.
  3. Abandoned cart reminders: while a customer fills in the checkout, only if email alerts are enabled and the customer has given permission (ticked the checkbox, or is a logged-in returning customer who was informed and did not opt out). What is sent: the customer’s email address and first name, the products and quantities in the cart, the cart total and currency, the text of the permission shown and the time. Ailoquence uses it to send a single reminder email with a link that restores the cart; every email includes an unsubscribe link. Nothing is sent for customers who do not give permission.
  • Terms and conditions: https://ailoquence.com/terms-and-conditions/
  • Privacy policy: https://ailoquence.com/privacy-policy/
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin, search for “Ailoquence Connector”, then click Install Now and Activate.
  2. Open the new Ailoquence menu in your WordPress admin. You will see a Public Key and a Secret generated for your site.
  3. In Ailoquence, open your project, go to the Blog settings, add your site’s URL and paste the Public Key and Secret. Save and check the connection.

To connect your WooCommerce store:

  1. In Ailoquence, add an ecommerce store to your project and paste the Store Public Key and Store Secret from the plugin’s settings page. Save the project.
  2. Back in WordPress, click Connect my store automatically.
sections.faq:
Do I need an Ailoquence account?

Yes. The plugin is the bridge between your site and Ailoquence; it has no features of its own without an account. You can sign up at https://app.ailoquence.com/register.

Does the plugin work without WooCommerce?

Yes. WooCommerce is only needed if you want to link your store. Blog publishing works on any WordPress site.

Ailoquence says my credentials are wrong.

Make sure you copied the full Public Key and Secret, without spaces, and that “Accept requests from Ailoquence” is checked. If you filled in “Allowed IPs”, clear it and try again. If you regenerated your credentials, paste the new ones in Ailoquence.

My posts are published at the wrong time.

Scheduled posts use the time zone set in Settings > General. Check that it matches your local time zone.

Does it work with my SEO plugin?

Yes. With Yoast SEO, Rank Math or All in One SEO active, the SEO title, meta description, focus keyword and social tags are saved in that plugin, so you can review them in its usual box when editing the post. With any other SEO plugin, the Ailoquence Connector leaves the page alone to avoid duplicate tags. Without an SEO plugin, it adds the title, description, Open Graph, Twitter and schema.org tags itself.

What happens when I uninstall the plugin?

The plugin settings are deleted and the WooCommerce key created for Ailoquence is revoked. Your posts, images and categories are kept.
sections.changelog:
0.3.0

  • New: abandoned cart reminders. The checkout (block and classic) asks customers for permission to email them a reminder; the reminder link restores their cart.
  • New: “Email alerts from Ailoquence” setting to turn off all email alerts for the store from WordPress.
  • Privacy policy text suggestion under Settings → Privacy.
  • Fix: orders placed from the block checkout reached Ailoquence without their data (WooCommerce 10.3+ could not build the webhook body), so they did not count for sales, review requests or recovered carts.

0.2.1

  • New: choose the author of the posts published from Ailoquence (Post author setting). It defaults to the administrator who activated the plugin.
  • Fix: posts published from Ailoquence were created without an author.
  • The “Open Ailoquence” link on the settings page now goes straight to the Ailoquence app.
  • Updated the installation steps: install the plugin from Plugins > Add New Plugin.
  • Requires WordPress 5.9 or later.

0.2.0

  • Prepared for the WordPress.org plugin directory: English base texts, translatable, Spanish translation included.
  • New: step-by-step instructions on the settings page.
  • New: the WooCommerce key is revoked when you reconnect, disconnect the store or uninstall the plugin.
  • New: “Allowed IPs” ignores invalid addresses instead of blocking every request.
  • Fix: “Accept requests from Ailoquence” could not be turned off.
  • Fix: the Ailoquence connection ID was not saved after connecting the store.
  • Fix: backslashes in post content were lost when publishing.
  • Fix: the SEO title, description, keywords and social tags sent by Ailoquence were not saved. They are now written to Yoast SEO, Rank Math or All in One SEO, or output by the plugin when no SEO plugin is active.
  • Security: the public status endpoint no longer exposes your WordPress version.
  • Security: media uploads only accept images.
  • Security: removed a developer-only setting that allowed changing the Ailoquence API address.

0.1.3

  • Fix: scheduled posts are published in the site’s time zone.
